what: Broadridge runs the plumbing of investing. It processes proxy votes and shareholder communications for most US public companies, handles trade processing for brokers, and provides technology to wealth managers.
customers: Banks, brokers, asset and wealth managers, public companies and mutual funds.
money: proxy distribution, shareholder communications and regulatory mailings
trade processing, post-trade and wealth management platforms
moat: A near-monopoly on US proxy distribution, built on contracts with brokers who hold shares on behalf of investors, which no competitor has been able to break.
risks: Growth of about 9% is steady rather than fast
Debt of about $3.6 billion against almost no cash
Regulators periodically review proxy fee structures
opportunities: Return on invested capital of 16% with recurring revenue renewing at very high rates
Growth in retail investor accounts increases the volume of communications it handles
A dividend raised every year since it was spun out of ADP
watch: Recurring revenue growth and closed sales.
